title: rice.json
description: Settings for the desktop. Everything under "animation" is re-read while the bar is running, so saving this file shows the change on the next frame. The rest is read at startup.

ipc_url.description: GlazeWM's IPC socket. Use 127.0.0.1, never localhost: localhost resolves to ::1 first and every connection then burns ~2.1s waiting for the IPv6 attempt to time out.

bar_height.description: Status bar height in pixels. The workspace slide animation leaves this many rows alone so the bar does not move with the desktop. Read at startup: restart the bar after changing it.

mics.description: Substrings matched against capture-device names. micswitch cycles through the matching devices in this order.

outputs.description: Substrings matched against playback-device names, in the order they appear in the island's device page. A whitelist, not the full list: this machine reports 29 playback endpoints and nearly all are virtual (six RODE UNIFY buses, VB-Cable, VoiceMeeter, Steam Streaming, Oculus, NVIDIA Broadcast), which would bury the real ones. Bluetooth audio devices are always listed regardless, so a newly paired headset appears without editing this.

clickthrough_apps.description: Executables that make the bar click-through while focused, matched case-insensitively. The geometric test covers true fullscreen; borderless games that sit a few pixels short of the monitor rect slip past it, so those need naming here.

hide_bar_on_fullscreen.description: Hide the bar while a fullscreen application covers its monitor. It used to only go click-through there: still drawn, still on top of the game, just not clickable. Notifications are the exception -- the island still appears over a game, because the point of a notification is to be seen. Set false to go back to a bar that is always drawn.

index_store_apps.description: Include Store/UWP apps in the index. Off by default: they drag in a long tail that is not really applications (settings pages, help links, 'Visit <vendor>' web shortcuts), and each can only be started indirectly through its AUMID, which also means it can never be launched elevated. The cost of leaving them out is real: anything shipping ONLY as a packaged app becomes unfindable, which on this machine includes Claude and Windows Terminal.

index_files.description: Search files as well as applications. The launcher builds its own index rather than using the Windows Search service: WSearch costs 218 MB, covers ~196k of this machine's ~2.17M entries (it excludes AppData, every dotfolder and all of D:), and has no infix matching, so a fuzzy launcher cannot sit on it. Off means nothing is walked and nothing is held.

file_roots.description: What the file index covers. Empty means every fixed drive, which includes the profile via C:. Spell roots out to NARROW the index, e.g. ["C:\\Users\\obisp", "D:\\"].

file_skip.description: Directory paths the walk refuses to descend into, matched as case-insensitive suffixes of the full path -- '\node_modules' catches it at any depth, '\.cargo\registry' only the one below .cargo. The defaults are 500,079 of the profile's 1,394,364 entries on this machine. Add '\windows' and '\program files' here to trade findability for about 30 MB.

file_limit.description: Ceiling on indexed entries, not a target. Exists so a network drive or a runaway junction cannot turn the index into an out-of-memory bug.

animation.description: Motion tuning. Live-reloaded: edit, save, watch.

spring_stiffness.description: Stiffness of the island's vertical bubble spring. Higher is snappier.

spring_damping.description: Damping of that spring. What matters is damping / (2 * sqrt(stiffness)): below 1.0 it overshoots and bounces, at 1.0 it glides in without overshooting. The default works out to 0.66 = one clear bounce. Near 0.6 it rings several times; near 0.75 the overshoot is a few pixels and reads as no bounce at all.

pill_ease.description: How fast the pill itself resizes, as an exponential rate. Higher is faster. Does not overshoot.

text_ease.description: How fast the clock travels and scales as the island opens. Deliberately separate from the spring: the shape may bounce, the text may not, because letters visibly wobbling read as a glitch.

workspace_ease.description: How fast the focused-workspace highlight slides between workspace numbers.

notification_hold_secs.description: Seconds a notification stays in the island before collapsing.

panel_timeout_secs.description: Seconds without interaction before an open island panel closes itself.

spectrum_fps.description: Frame rate of the audio spectrum while sound plays. This is the bar's main CPU lever, being the only thing that repaints continuously: measured on a 2560px bar, 60fps cost about 8% of a core and 30fps costs about 1%, with no visible difference.
